- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.10) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reverts toward recent 7–14 day average; if model is >1.5σ above mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.15, apply 70% weight to recent price; if <0.05, apply 30% weight to 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.22, -0.28), model underperforms; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to compensate for risk aversion.
